survivingClaim: Precise obstruction, no statement about zeros of zeta. On theta restricted to the arc of X_0(4)(R), T_{p^2} has 2 real and p^2+p-2 complex isogenous points (outside a countable set of x); the summed complex points equal theta - p^{-2} D_{p^{-2}} theta + p^{-1}(theta - D_{p^2} theta), positive on the arc, with Mellin multiplier C_p = 1+1/p-R_p, R_p = 2p^{-3/2}cosh((s-1/2)log p); the relation is the identity c(pm)=c(m); C_p*Lambda is -p^{-3/2} times the T-NR twin with c=-(p^{3/2}+p^{1/2}) and every T-NR twin lies in the same module; the algebra <D_l, W> acts on a W-fixed vector through a+bW -> a+b (Dirichlet polynomials); termwise bounds on complex points lose (p-1)p^{-1/2}; the second moment over the points tau+b/p is Theta_{L+}+Theta_{L-}-theta(p^2 x)^2 (map row G16). Controls: T-NR and E_a pass every step; Epstein n=5,6 and DH fail only at the multiplicativity identity; twists fail at the Fricke step. MEASURED only (float, confirmed by a second method, not enclosed): off-line zeros of the p=5 single-point function and of the Epstein zeta of [2,2,5]. The device is closed for the four listed forms; all identities are classical.

Closed for the four listed forms; not excluded: a functional of unsummed complex points that is neither linear nor a second moment.

lesson: Base-side loading on the oval adds no input. Summing the complex isogenous points over b projects onto dilates of theta, so every Hecke statement on the arc is a multiplier times Lambda. A non-commutative Hecke/Fricke algebra acting on a Fricke-fixed vector collapses to its commutative dilation part, and M_{1/2}(Gamma_0(4)) is one-dimensional. The complex-point term is itself a T-NR twin. A device on this arc must read something that E_a and T-NR lack, i.e. the size of the Hecke eigenvalue.
